data.content_ref: inline:SRC_004 and SRC_005 share a mechanism: positive cut thickness (or pathological curves) changes the topological count by destroying or fragmenting the center region. SRC_004 projects this to infinity via fractal cuts; SRC_005 projects it to a center-singularity that may disconnect the 8 sectors. They abstract a common principle: when cut width is non-zero the center is no longer a shared boundary, and the count is no longer 8. This is REFUTED IF a finite-thickness model with four straight concurrent cuts yields exactly 8 disconnected pieces with no center-removal effect — which would mean thickness alone, without fractal geometry, is insufficient to change the count, breaking the shared mechanism.
